## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix the JSON option parsing before merge because placing `--json` before `--junit` can prevent either requested report from being written.

## Changes

The pull request adds `--json` with an optional destination that defaults to `results.json`, and adds a function that writes reports to the parsed destinations. It also adds parser and file-writing tests.

## Critical

- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Preserve flags after a bare `--json` — `--json --junit report.xml` consumes `--junit` as the JSON destination and rejects `report.xml` as an unknown option. The lookahead checks only whether another token exists. — Putting `--json` first prevents users from generating either report. — Fix: Consume the next argument as a destination only if it exists and does not start with `--`.

## Important

- app/cli.py:30 — correctness — Reject shared report destinations before writing — `--junit results.json --json` sends both reports to `results.json`. The second `write_text` call overwrites the JUnit report with JSON. — The command returns successfully, but a downstream JUnit reader receives JSON. — Fix: Validate that the destinations are distinct before writing either report.

## Suggestions

- app/cli.py:29 — tests — Cover writing both reports to distinct paths — The `--json report.json --junit report.xml` path reaches a second loop iteration that no test exercises. The only writer test requests JSON alone. — A regression that stops writing after the first report would pass the suite. — Fix: Extend `test_json_default_and_explicit_path` to check both output files in one call.
